solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tale of woe from Fisher never-ending, I notice

indicators.note: the name loses its final letter, as never-ending says it has no end

parts.note: Jeremy Fisher is the frog in Beatrix Potter's tale
a notice is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone notices a long-running lament coming from an angler who won't stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' drops the last letter of JEREMY, leaving JEREM. Mr Jeremy Fisher is a Beatrix Potter frog who goes fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long mournful complaint, named after the prophet Jeremiah's Lamentations.

clue.text: Takes part in tournament, with lowest score placed last? Exactly

indicators.note: the score letter is shifted from its place to the very end of the word

parts.note: knights in a tournament joust, so takes part = jousts
the lowest score is nil, written as O

explanation.surface: A knight competing in a tournament finishes bottom of the table, and someone confirms it precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed last' moves the O of JOUSTS to the end, giving JUSTS O.
explanation.definitionFit: Just so is an idiom of agreement meaning precisely, quite right.

clue.text: Transport losing time in monsoon

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the transport word

parts.note: trains are a form of transport

explanation.surface: Rail services lose time when the monsoon arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes T from TRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: The monsoon is the seasonal period of heavy downpours in South Asia.

clue.text: Getting entangled in church service good for son

indicators.note: good for son means the G replaces the S

parts.note: mattins (also matins) is the Anglican morning service
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone gets tangled up during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for son' swaps the S at the end of MATTINS for G. Mattins is the older double-T spelling of matins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fibres that are matting are twisting into a dense tangle.

clue.text: Corrupt characters from USA, East Bengal, that Labour cleaned out

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters are spoiled and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Crooked people from America and East Bengal are the ones a political party purged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges USA EAST BENGAL. Labour is a Herculean task, not the British political party, which the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules's fifth task was to clean King Augeas's filthy cattle stalls in a single day.

clue.text: Islanders caught by embargo America maintains

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: maintains means holds or supports, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: US is short for United States, America
an embargo is a ban

explanation.surface: People from an island are hit by a trade embargo that the United States keeps in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintains' signals one piece held within another. The surface points neatly at the long-running American embargo on Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubans are the people of the Caribbean island nation of Cuba.

clue.text: Parvenu's new business the wrong way round

indicators.note: the two halves of the business term are swapped round, back half to the front

parts.note: a new business is a start-up

explanation.surface: A newly rich person's fresh company is being run backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' moves UP from the end of STARTUP to the front. The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone who has risen suddenly in wealth or status, a social climber.

clue.text: Article on musical cat pronounced heavenly

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: pronounced says we take the word as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: the Jellicle cats appear in the musical Cats, from T. S. Eliot's poems

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a cat in a musical calls it divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' signals that JELLICLE, the Cats musical's feline tribe, is heard as GELICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelical is an old-fashioned form of angelic, belonging to the angels and heaven.

clue.text: Overarching panel plans red revolt

indicators.note: a revolt overturns order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A committee covering everything plots a communist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolt' rearranges PLANS RED. 'Overarching panel' reads like an oversight committee but is literal: the panel beside an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a spandrel is the roughly triangular wall area between the curve of an arch and its frame.

clue.text: Penniless, proper not to start clinging

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

indicators.note: the word for proper loses its opening letter

parts.note: right means proper, correct

explanation.surface: A broke but respectable person refuses to start being clingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' drops the R of RIGHT, leaving IGHT. SKINT is everyday British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Skintight clothing fits so closely that it hugs the body.

clue.text: A companion to Don Giovanni, I felt, caught me out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the seducer Don Giovanni's friend took them by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I FELT CAUGHT ME. 'Companion' suggests a person, such as Leporello, but it means a fellow opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart composed both Don Giovanni and this opera, so it is a fitting partner work.

clue.text: Foreign character shortly put name to parent

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to put your name to something is to sign it
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An odd person is soon to sign a document naming a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the last letter from SIGN, leaving SIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character foreign to English.

clue.text: Poem in French is popular, widening appeal

indicators.note: the appeal letters are pushed apart to make room for others in the middle

parts.note: SA, short for sex appeal
est is the French for is
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A French poem is a hit, broadening its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widening' means the appeal abbreviation is stretched apart to hold the other pieces. SA for sex appeal is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a strict verse form of six six-line stanzas reusing the same six line-endings.

clue.text: Given message to stay away from edges with light

indicators.note: the word for stay is cut at both ends, its outer letters taken away

parts.note: to remain is to stay
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a light

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep away from the sides and bring a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from edges' removes the R and N from REMAIN, leaving EMAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been emailed has been sent an electronic message.

clue.text: Recent discovery of chap's piano piece netting two grand

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: his means belonging to a chap
G is slang for a grand, a thousand, so two make GG
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an article is a piece, as an item or a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A man's piano composition brings in two thousand pounds, which is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'netting' looks like earning money, which suits the surface, but it signals a container. G for grand (a thousand) is slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Higgs boson was confirmed at CERN in 2012, a recent finding in physics.

clue.text: Chief nobleman and a number of his staff?

parts.note: head means chief, as in head chef
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A senior aristocrat and how many servants he keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the tally of a nobleman's household.
explanation.definitionFit: A headcount is the total number of people, especially employees, on the payroll.

clue.text: Grains turned up for breakfast, for a limited period

definitions.text: Grains turned up for breakfast, for a limited period

parts.words: Grains turned up for breakfast, for a limited period
parts.note: sand grains in a small hourglass, turned over at breakfast to time a boiled egg for a few minutes

explanation.surface: A cereal is on the breakfast menu only for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grains' and 'breakfast' point at cereal, but these are sand grains in a kitchen hourglass.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sand-glass runs for about three minutes, the time needed to soft-boil an egg.

clue.text: Chair here obstacle an ignorant lad's damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An uneducated boy has broken a chair, which got in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges AN IGNORANT LAD. This famous British steeplechase is run at Aintree, and The Chair is one of its fences.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chair is a tall fence jumped by horses in this race, so it is an obstacle there.

clue.text: Most determined to make uniform, then relax

parts.note: do means make, as in do a drawing
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
rest means relax

explanation.surface: A very resolute person tells others to put on uniforms and then take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dourest is the superlative of dour, meaning stern and stubbornly unyielding.

clue.text: Striking reason to eat off one's knees?

definitions.meaning: striking means remarkable, worthy of note

definitions.text: reason to eat off one's knees?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, the lack of a dining surface makes you rest your plate on your lap

explanation.surface: A noteworthy excuse for eating a meal on your lap.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after NO and the second reading appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable stands out and deserves attention, as a striking thing does.

clue.text: Magistrate's about to arrest a ruler of the waves

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the reversed word grips the next letter
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice; doge's gives DOGES

explanation.surface: A judge is going to detain someone who rules the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses DOGES into SEGOD, and 'to arrest' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon or Neptune, a deity of the sea, rules the waves.

clue.text: Opening of tale genuine and touching

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: actual means genuine, real

explanation.surface: The start of a story is real and moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like emotionally moving, but it means relating to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactual means relating to the sense of touch, tactile.

clue.text: Weary and greasy, I assume ship has to leave

parts.note: fat food is greasy

indicators.note: the ship letters must leave the word for assume

parts.note: to guess is to assume
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A tired, grubby sailor supposes the ship must depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to leave' takes SS out of GUESS, leaving GUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fatigue someone is to tire them out, so the verb means to wear out.

clue.text: Sound investment may be shown in court

indicators.note: sound says the word is said aloud and the answer is what we hear

parts.note: gilts are British government bonds, a safe investment

explanation.surface: A safe investment might be displayed as evidence in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'safe', describing the investment, but it is the homophone signal. Gilts are UK government bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant's culpability may be proved or revealed during a trial.

clue.text: Timid person I click with?

definitions.meaning: a shy, nervous person, as quiet as a small rodent
the pointing device that a computer user clicks

explanation.surface: A shy person says they get on well with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'click with' suggests getting on well, but it is the computer device speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer pointer device is clicked, and a timid soul is a proverbial small rodent.

clue.text: Moving unsteadily, part of body initially being secured in strap

indicators.note: secured in means held fast inside, so these letters sit within the strap

parts.note: a sling is a strap, as for a rifle or arm
tum is a colloquial word for stomach

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word being

explanation.surface: An injured person staggers about with their arm held in a sling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured in' places the stomach word and the B from 'initially being' inside the strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stumbling trips and lurches as they walk.

clue.text: Shoddy stuff, breaking eggs to make revolution

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so one word is broken by another inside it

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
tat is cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: Cheap goods cracking eggs is presented as a recipe for revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' signals a container. 'revolution' suggests an uprising but means a turn about an axis.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn round an axis, making a full turn.

clue.text: Traveller ate wrongly — did it again

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
eated is an incorrect, childish past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A salesman eats carelessly and does it a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' looks like an anagram signal for ATE, but EATED is the mistaken past tense of eat, as a child might say.
explanation.definitionFit: To have repeated something is to have done it once more.
